Which company would you invest in Company A or Company B if they had the same rev, same growth, same industry however Company A had 10% EBITDA margin vs Company B’s 20% EBITDA margin?
Walk me through the changes in the 3 financial statements if deferred wages are up by $100M
questions.answer:
IS: Salaries expense up by $100M. Assuming a 40% tax rate, NI is down by $60M
CF: NI is down by $60M but since the salaries expense is non-cash we add it back to our CFFO which means that our CFFO is up by $40M. No other changes which means that our overall cash is up by $40M.
BS: Assets – Cash up by $40M
Liabilities – Salaries Payable is up by $100M
Shareholders’ Equity – NI is down by $60M which flows into our Retained Earnings. Thus, both sides balance being up by $40M.

questions.question: Walk me through the changes in the 3 financial statements if we sold an asset with a book value of $10M book value for a $6M gain
questions.answer:
IS: Gain on Sale up by $6M, which means that our EBIT is up by $6M. Assuming a 20% tax rate, our NI is up by $4.8M.
CF: NI is up by $4.8M which flows into the top-line of our cash flow statement. No other changes to CFFO which means that our CFFO is up by $4.8M. There are no changes to CFFF. CFFI is up by $10M. Thus, overall our cash is up by $14.8M.
BS: Assets – Cash up by $14.8M, PP&E down by $10M which means that overall assets up by $4.8M. Liabilities – No changes Shareholders’ Equity – NI is up by $4.8M which flows into our Retained Earnings. Thus, both sides balance being up by $4.8M.
